Project arrivals to Minnesota ran from 1992 to 1996, then families reunited ([MPR, 2011](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2011/05/06/dalai-lama-setup)); a federal family reunification program began in 1997 ([Harvard Pluralism Project](https://hwpi.harvard.edu/pluralismarchive/gyuto-wheel-dharma-monastery)). Tibetans also moved here from other states. The exile population in South Asia has since fallen from about 150,000 to just over 100,000, partly because people moved on to North America, Australia and Europe ([MPI](https://www.migrationpolicy.org/node/17894)).

sections.heading: Minnesota History
sections.body:
Thupten Dadak, one of two Tibetans in Minnesota in 1985 ([MPR, 2001](https://news.minnesota.publicradio.org/features/200105/07_newsroom_dalai/culture.shtml); MNopedia gives 1986), was appointed in 1990 by the Office of the Dalai Lama to coordinate Twin Cities resettlement ([Hennepin History Museum](https://hennepinhistory.org/?p=7699)).

- 1992: TAFM founded in St. Paul; it merged with the Tibetan Association of Minnesota after the Dalai Lama’s May 2001 visit, and bought 1096 Raymond Avenue in 2003 ([MNopedia](https://www.mnhs.org/mnopedia/search/index/group/tibetan-american-foundation-minnesota-tafm)).
- 1994: Gyuto Wheel of Dharma Monastery established ([Harvard](https://hwpi.harvard.edu/pluralismarchive/gyuto-wheel-dharma-monastery)).
- 1997 and 2008: Tibetan Cultural School and Lamton founded ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/about-us/)).
- 2005: MNHS recorded 22 oral histories ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/minnesota-immigrant-oral-histories/collections.mnhs.org/ioh/10000814.html)).
- 2020: TAFM bought its Isanti building ([County Star](https://www.isanti-chisagocountystar.com/news/music-dance-tradition-highlight-dalai-lama-birthday-celebration/article_d6ac31a2-25a7-44dc-b24c-7054fb384fc4.html)).
- 2023 to 2025: exhibit “Faraway Home: Tibetans in Minnesota” ([Hennepin History Museum](https://hennepinhistory.org/?p=7699)).

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Resettlement shaped family life directly. Because only one family member could apply under the 1990 project, spouses and children often waited about three years to join the first arrival ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/minnesota-immigrant-oral-histories/collections.mnhs.org/ioh/10000907.html)). Many households therefore include members who arrived at different times, from different countries and through different immigration routes, alongside children born in Minnesota.

Ask who lives in the household, whom the person wants involved in decisions, and who should receive information. Do not assume that relatives share a family name, a birthplace, a first language or an immigration history. Some relatives may still live in India, Nepal or Tibet, and obligations across borders may matter to a budget or plan, so ask.

sections.heading: Religion
sections.body:
Tibetan Buddhism and Bon are the major religions of Tibet ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/becoming-minnesotan/education.mnhs.org/immigration/communities/tibetan.html)). Tibetan Buddhism includes the Gelug, Nyingma, Sakya and Kagyu traditions; the Gyuto Wheel of Dharma Monastery is Gelug, and Harvard’s Pluralism Project reported that many Tibetans practice mainly at home ([Harvard, updated 2015](https://hwpi.harvard.edu/pluralismarchive/gyuto-wheel-dharma-monastery)).

The monastery has moved: MPR placed it on Minnehaha Avenue in 2007 ([MPR](https://archive.mpr.org/stories/2007/05/11/minnesotas-tibetan-monks-chant-for-their-homeland)), Harvard in Columbia Heights, and a 2019 report at 26th Avenue and Taylor Street in Minneapolis ([Northeaster](https://mynortheaster.com/news/local-tibetans-focus-on-future-in-northeast)), so confirm the current address. TAFM arranges Buddhist rituals and prayers for members facing illness or loss ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/programs/social-service)). Ask about practice only when it bears on care, scheduling or end of life, and do not assume a level of observance.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
Tibetan is a Tibeto-Burman language with its own alphabet, derived from an Indian script of the Gupta era. Central, Khams and Amdo Tibetan share a literary language, and about 150,000 exiles speak a standard based on Central Tibetan; Dzongkha, Sikkimese, Sherpa and Balti are separate languages ([University of Oxford](https://orinst.web.ox.ac.uk/tibetan)). In Tibetan areas under Chinese rule, Mandarin is the official language ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/becoming-minnesotan/education.mnhs.org/immigration/communities/tibetan.html)).

### Booking an interpreter

Book Tibetan, ask which spoken form the person uses, and confirm early that the interpreter and the person understand each other. Mandarin, Hindi and Nepali are not substitutes, even when the person speaks them. Follow qualified-interpreter and CLAS requirements, do not use children, and plan telephone or video backup.

### Literacy

Some people read Tibetan script, some English, Hindi or Nepali. Ask how the person prefers written information, and explain key notices aloud.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
sections.body:
Tibetan names often do not fit the first-name, last-name structure of forms. Minnesota sources say little about naming beyond one point: in 2001, at least three-quarters of about two dozen students in one Twin Cities Tibetan dance group were named Tenzin, after the Dalai Lama ([MPR, 2001](https://news.minnesota.publicradio.org/features/200105/07_newsroom_dalai/culture.shtml)). Shared names are common.

Do not assume that the second part of a name is an inherited surname, that relatives share it, or that a name shows gender. Ask how the person wants to be addressed and how the name appears on the document your program uses, record it exactly, and note any preferred name. Never merge or match records on name alone, and do not reorder names to fit a screen.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
The white khata, a ceremonial scarf, is offered at celebrations, and khatas and incense are used at births, weddings, funerals, graduations, and the arrival or departure of guests ([MPR, 2019](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2019/07/06/tibetan-americans-minneapolis-celebration)). You may see one offered at a community event or a meeting with community leaders.

Introduce yourself plainly, ask how the person would like to be addressed, and follow their lead on handshakes and other contact. If you are offered a khata, accepting it graciously is respectful; you do not need to bring one. With elders, take time over the introduction and confirm through the interpreter that the purpose of the visit was understood.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Public sources give little Minnesota-specific guidance on etiquette, so the most useful habit is to ask. On a home visit, notice whether shoes are left at the door, or ask. Do not touch or photograph a household shrine without permission. If a monk or lama is present, ask the family how they would like the meeting arranged.

Harvard reported in 2015 that visitors were invited to observe Sunday evening prayers at the Gyuto monastery ([Harvard](https://hwpi.harvard.edu/pluralismarchive/gyuto-wheel-dharma-monastery)); confirm current practice and attend as a guest, not for work.

An early organizer described Tibetans in 2001 as “always a little conservative” ([MPR](https://news.minnesota.publicradio.org/features/200105/07_newsroom_dalai/culture.shtml)). That is one person’s view, not a rule. A quiet response may mean politeness, uncertainty or a language barrier, so check understanding with open questions.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
sections.body:
Most religious observances follow the Tibetan lunar calendar, so their dates move each year; confirm them annually with a partner.

- Losar, the Tibetan New Year: February 7 in 2027 ([University of Maine](https://umaine.edu/religious-studies/?p=1522)), long celebrated in St. Paul in late February or March ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/becoming-minnesotan/education.mnhs.org/immigration/communities/tibetan.html)).
- Saga Dawa: the fourth lunar month, honoring the Buddha’s birth, enlightenment and passing ([Norbulingka](https://www.norbulingka.org/blogs/our-journal/saga-dawa)).
- Lhabab Duechen: the ninth lunar month; and March 10, Tibetan Uprising Day, on the Gregorian calendar ([MNopedia](https://www.mnhs.org/mnopedia/search/index/group/tibetan-american-foundation-minnesota-tafm)).
- July 6: the Dalai Lama’s birthday ([MPR, 2019](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2019/07/06/tibetan-americans-minneapolis-celebration)).
- December: anniversary of the Dalai Lama’s 1989 Nobel Peace Prize ([Harvard](https://hwpi.harvard.edu/pluralismarchive/gyuto-wheel-dharma-monastery); [MPR, 2011](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2011/05/06/dalai-lama-setup)).

Check before scheduling hearings, listening sessions or deadlines near these dates.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
Tibetan adults raised in exile may have attended schools affiliated with the Central Tibetan Administration, where enrollment fell 39 percent between 2000 and 2023 ([MPI](https://www.migrationpolicy.org/node/17894)).

In Minnesota, the Tibetan Cultural School, founded in 1997, teaches children Tibetan language, history, religion and heritage, and Lamton, founded in 2008 by Tibetan students at Carleton and St. Olaf, mentors teenagers toward higher education ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/about-us/)). Classes run from preschool through eighth grade ([MNopedia](https://www.mnhs.org/mnopedia/search/index/group/tibetan-american-foundation-minnesota-tafm)). TAFM’s founder said in 2023, “when you’ve lost your language, you’ve lost your identity” ([Star Tribune](https://www.startribune.com/minnesotan-tibetan-history-heritage-is-the-focus-of-new-hennepin-history-museum-exhibit-faraway-home/600288545)).

Ask each parent which language they want for school meetings and documents, and do not infer schooling from birthplace.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
No Tibetan-specific Minnesota health rates are cited here, and none should be assumed. Public sources show community health work instead: the Tibetan Nurses Association, a TAFM partner, focuses on community health ([MNopedia](https://www.mnhs.org/mnopedia/search/index/group/tibetan-american-foundation-minnesota-tafm)), and TAFM coordinates free flu shots with local hospitals and supports families during illness or death ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/programs/social-service)).

Sowa Rigpa, the Tibetan medical system, is taught at Men-Tsee-Khang in Dharamsala, and the University of Minnesota’s Center for Spirituality and Healing has run a Tibetan Healing Initiative since 2005 ([Men-Tsee-Khang](https://dcollege.mentseekhang.org/a-six-day-initiative-program-between-men-tsee-khang-college-and-the-center-for-spirituality-healing-university-of-minnesota/)). Ask, without judgment, whether a person uses traditional remedies alongside other care. Exile histories can include dangerous journeys and long separations; do not ask people to retell them.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Public sources about Tibetan Minnesota say nothing specific about LGBTQ community members, and this page does not speculate. LGBTQ Tibetan Minnesotans may be part of any household you serve.

The Minnesota Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination in public services, employment, housing and other areas on grounds including sexual orientation and gender identity ([Minnesota Department of Human Rights](https://mn.gov/mdhr/yourrights/mhra/)). Use the name and pronouns a person gives you. Do not ask relatives about anyone’s sexuality or gender, and do not share what a person tells you unless a rule requires it. In a small community, ask whether the person is comfortable with the assigned interpreter.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
Traditional Tibetan clothing appears at community celebrations, such as the folk dance that opened the 2019 birthday gathering at Boom Island Park; the same report describes prayer flags, whose colors stand for natural elements ([MPR](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2019/07/06/tibetan-americans-minneapolis-celebration)). Gyuto monks wear wine-colored robes ([MPR, 2007](https://archive.mpr.org/stories/2007/05/11/minnesotas-tibetan-monks-chant-for-their-homeland)).

Everyday dress varies by person, age and occasion, and sources say little more. Ask before touching a person or a religious item they wear, and do not read dress as a measure of faith. If a person asks for a same-gender clinician or interpreter for personal care, handle it like any other accommodation request.

sections.heading: Music, Literature, and Art
sections.body:
Classical Tibetan is the main literary language, especially for Buddhist texts, and its spelling has changed little since the seventh century ([University of Oxford](https://orinst.web.ox.ac.uk/tibetan)). Gyuto monks are known for tantric chanting, performed at the Basilica of Saint Mary in 2007 ([MPR](https://archive.mpr.org/stories/2007/05/11/minnesotas-tibetan-monks-chant-for-their-homeland)).

In Minnesota, the Ü-Tsang Dance Group had performed for 25 years by 2023, and monks from Tashi Kyil Monastery made a mandala at the opening of the Hennepin History Museum exhibit ([Mpls.St.Paul Magazine](https://mspmag.com/arts-and-culture/hennepin-history-museum-opens-local-tibetan-exhibit/)). TAFM offers weekend performing arts classes for ages 7 to 18 and an instrument program ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/about-us/)), and has raised funds for youth Tibetan opera ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/)).

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
TAFM lists sports and youth development among its programs, and its plans for the Isanti site include a basketball facility for young people ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/about-us/)). Public sources say little else about Tibetan sports in Minnesota.

Youth sports and recreation can be good places to share information about services when a community organization invites you, but they are not a substitute for language access or direct outreach. Do not assume a person’s interests from what an organization offers.

sections.heading: Work and Business
sections.body:
In 2011, TAFM said a large share of the community worked in health care ([MPR](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2011/05/06/dalai-lama-setup)), and the resettlement project required each applicant to have a job lined up before arrival ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/minnesota-immigrant-oral-histories/collections.mnhs.org/ioh/10000907.html)). Tibetan-owned businesses have included a Tibetan cultural store in Minneapolis ([Hennepin History Museum](https://hennepinhistory.org/?p=7699)) and, from 2018, the first Tibetan-owned restaurant in Northeast Minneapolis ([Northeaster, 2019](https://mynortheaster.com/news/local-tibetans-focus-on-future-in-northeast)).

Do not assume a person’s occupation from group patterns. Ask about credentials earned in India or Nepal, which may need recognition here, and about shift schedules when setting appointments. Tibetan colleagues are coworkers, not the agency’s interpreter pool.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
Start with language: ask which language the person wants, book a qualified Tibetan interpreter where that is the answer, and confirm the spoken form works. Do not use a child or relative for sensitive topics, even when the family offers, and ask whether the person is comfortable with the interpreter assigned.

A document may list India, Nepal or China as a birthplace. Record it accurately, offer self-identification where the form allows, and never describe a person as Chinese, Indian or Nepali on the basis of a document. Do not ask about politics or about how someone left Tibet.

At serious illness or end of life, ask whether the person or family wants religious rites, a monk or lama present, or support from TAFM ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/programs/social-service)).

sections.heading: Adjacent Communities
sections.body:
Some pages in this app may seem close, but a Tibetan household should not be routed to them by default.

- Chinese Minnesota (chinese): a document may say China, and Mandarin is official in Tibetan areas under Chinese rule ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/becoming-minnesotan/education.mnhs.org/immigration/communities/tibetan.html)), but Tibetan identity and language are distinct, and a 2008 Tibetan protest in St. Paul drew public disagreement from a member of the local Chinese community ([MPR, 2008](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2008/04/10/tibetans-hold-vigil-in-st-paul)). Do not book Mandarin or apply that page.
- Indian (Asian Indian) Minnesota (indian): many Tibetans were born or schooled in India, but Hindi is not their home language and that page describes a different people.

The app has no Nepali, Bhutanese, Sherpa or Mongolian page, and Dzongkha, Sikkimese and Sherpa are separate from Tibetan ([Oxford](https://orinst.web.ox.ac.uk/tibetan)). Book the language each household names, and let people of mixed heritage say which page applies.

sections.heading: Counts and Statistics
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass has no Tibetan profile ([Minnesota Compass](https://www.mncompass.org/cultural-communities)); it profiles only groups with at least 175 unweighted ACS records, identified by race, Hispanic origin, ancestry or birthplace ([Compass methodology](https://mncompass.org/demographics/cultural-communities/methodology)). The state demographer’s June 2026 chart of Asian Pacific groups above 1,000 people, from the 2024 ACS, has no Tibetan line either ([State Demographic Center](https://mn.gov/capm/assets/SusanBrower_StateOfAsianPacificMinnesotans_June2026_tcm1051-759113.pdf)). This page therefore gives no ACS count or margin of error for Tibetan Minnesotans.

### Community estimates, dated

- About 1,000 in 2001 ([MPR](https://news.minnesota.publicradio.org/features/200105/07_newsroom_dalai/culture.shtml)); more than 1,300 in 2005 ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/minnesota-immigrant-oral-histories/collections.mnhs.org/ioh/10000907.html)).
- 2,500 to 3,000 in 2011, per TAFM ([MPR](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2011/05/06/dalai-lama-setup)).
- About 3,500 as of 2019, per community members ([MNopedia](https://www.mnhs.org/mnopedia/search/index/group/tibetan-american-foundation-minnesota-tafm)); closer to 5,000 in 2023, per TAFM’s founder ([Star Tribune](https://www.startribune.com/minnesotan-tibetan-history-heritage-is-the-focus-of-new-hennepin-history-museum-exhibit-faraway-home/600288545)).

### What the counts are not

They use different boundaries and methods, and none is a census. Refugee tables miss the immigrant-visa founders; MDH’s 2016 slides fold Tibet into “Other” ([MDH](https://health.state.mn.us/communities/rih/stats/2016data.pdf)). Birthplace may read India, Nepal or China.

sections.heading: Resources
sections.body:
- Tibetan American Foundation of Minnesota: cultural school, Lamton, performing arts, social and spiritual services, and an immigration assistance program, by its own description; 1096 Raymond Ave., St. Paul, and 1321 Heritage Blvd. NE, Isanti ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/about-us/); [TAFM home](https://tafm.org/)).
- TAFM social and health services, in its own words ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/programs/social-service)), also in the state aging and disability resource directory ([Minnesota Aging and Disability Resources](https://mn.gov/adresources/search/8a0e9b0b-7f7f-5f48-b05a-3ffbb43e3c62)).
- Gyuto Wheel of Dharma Monastery ([Harvard Pluralism Project](https://hwpi.harvard.edu/pluralismarchive/gyuto-wheel-dharma-monastery)); confirm its address.
- MNopedia on TAFM ([MNHS](https://www.mnhs.org/mnopedia/search/index/group/tibetan-american-foundation-minnesota-tafm)) and MNHS oral histories ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/minnesota-immigrant-oral-histories/collections.mnhs.org/ioh/10000814.html)).
- Hennepin History Museum exhibit ([Faraway Home](https://hennepinhistory.org/?p=7699)).

Use these before asking a Tibetan colleague to explain, and pay organizations for work you ask of them.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
sections.body:
### Documents and status

Tibetans in India rely on a Registration Certificate to live, work and study there ([Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, 2015](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/1204606.html)). Indian-born children of Tibetan refugees born between 1950 and 1987 became eligible for Indian citizenship under a 2014 directive ([MPI](https://www.migrationpolicy.org/node/17894)), and the U.S. State Department said in 2021 that no Tibetans in Nepal had been registered since 1995 ([RFA](https://rfa.org/english/news/tibet/register-01272021183735.html)). The 1990s arrivals were treated as stateless persons rather than refugees ([MNHS](https://mnhs.gitlab.io/archive/becoming-minnesotan/education.mnhs.org/immigration/communities/tibetan.html)). Collect only what a program rule requires, and refer immigration questions to qualified legal help.

### Politics

Tibet’s status, the Dalai Lama’s succession ([TAFM](https://tafm.org/event/dalai-lamas-90th-birthday-year-to-be-celebrated-at-the-minnesota-state-capitol/)) and protest ([MPR, 2008](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2008/04/10/tibetans-hold-vigil-in-st-paul)) are live public questions. DHS staff should not raise them.

sections.heading: Connections to Human Services
sections.body:
### Language access

Offer Tibetan interpretation and translation, confirm the spoken form, follow qualified-interpreter and CLAS requirements, and arrange phone or video options ahead of time. Do not substitute Mandarin, Hindi or Nepali unless the person asks.

### Names in databases

Do not invent a surname or infer gender from a name. Names such as Tenzin are widely shared, so match records on required identifiers, never on name alone.

### Notices and outreach

Translate key notices into Tibetan and explain them aloud. A TAFM officer has translated census materials into Tibetan ([Northeaster](https://mynortheaster.com/news/local-tibetans-focus-on-future-in-northeast)) and is a natural outreach partner, as are the monastery and youth programs. Record who was actually reached.

### Greater Minnesota

TAFM’s Isanti center serves Isanti County ([Minnesota Aging and Disability Resources](https://mn.gov/adresources/search/8a0e9b0b-7f7f-5f48-b05a-3ffbb43e3c62)).

### Disability services and workforce

Sources say little about disability among Tibetan Minnesotans. Ask how the family describes the need, explain services in their language, and do not assume family will provide all care. Formal civil-rights or accommodation questions go to the responsible DHS office.
